dedupe_keys.name: christchurch 22 february 2011 earthquake lifeline performance and recovery

description: This case study covers how Christchurch's lifelines performed and were restored after the magnitude 6.3 earthquake of 22 February 2011, which caused 182 deaths and the largest lifeline disruption in a New Zealand city in 80 years, much of it from severe liquefaction, while networks were still recovering from the September 2010 Darfield earthquake. Giovinazzi and co-authors summarise physical damage, system performance and emergency and recovery management, focusing on gas, electricity and roads and on liquefaction ejecta clean-up, and highlight elements of resilience. A later study by Liu, Milke, Heiler and Giovinazzi analyses data on 33,000 sewer pipes and 13,000 repairs and renewals to show how CCTV damage data guided sewer reinstatement, and Bouziou and O'Rourke examine the water distribution system response. The NZSEE paper (December 2011) is available free under CC BY 4.0; the other two are journal articles whose access terms were not checked. Caveats: findings are specific to liquefaction-prone ground. It informs lifeline fragility, restoration and interdependency modelling for earthquake recovery planning; a related record is the HayWired lifeline collocation exposure dataset.
name: Christchurch 22 February 2011 earthquake, lifeline performance and recovery
outcomes: Documented lifeline damage and restoration, showing that ejecta clean-up and network management sped reinstatement and that damage data improved sewer recovery decisions.
provider: S. Giovinazzi, T. Wilson and co-authors (Bulletin of the NZ Society for Earthquake Engineering) and related studies
